assessment.security_status_cs: Saúdskoarabská koalice zahájila rozsáhlou vojenskou ofenzívu a masivní leteckou kampaní čítající 100 stíhaček dobyla zpět přístav Mocha a oblast úžiny Bab al-Mandab. assessment.security_status_en: The Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive and a massive air campaign involving 100 fighter jets, recapturing the port of Mocha and the Bab al-Mandab strait area. The conflict is escalating with the formation of new regional alliances (Makkah Alliance with Pakistan and Turkey) and threats of direct Houthi retaliatory attacks.

articles.title: Extreme heat warnings issued for parts of southern California
articles.summary:
Temperatures in US state forecast to hit high 30s celsius this week, while regions in Indonesia grapple with wildfires

The National Weather Service in the US has issued extreme heat warnings for parts of southern California, including Los Angeles, until Thursday, as temperatures are expected to hit the high 30s celsius. Burbank, a suburb north of Los Angeles, recorded 39C on Saturday, a few degrees shy of the October record for the region set in 1987. A persistent area of high pressure will remain in place this week, leading to further hazardous hot weather and increased fire risk.

Parts of Indonesia are in the midst of an extreme wildfire season, which has peaked over the past month. Western Kalimantan (Borneo) and southern Sumatra have been particularly badly affected. The lack of rainfall has dried the usually water-logged tropical soils, meaning that fires have been able to spread quickly, above and below the surface. Indonesia’s soils are also extremely rich in peat, meaning that the smoke produced from the fires contain higher levels of toxic gases such as sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide. Cities in surrounding areas and as far as Malaysia and Singapore have experienced reduced air quality in recent weeks as a result. Drought and wildfires are more common in this part of the world during El Niño events owing to suppressed thunderstorm activity.

Departure comes amid large drop in oil receipts, rampant inflation and shrinking economy

Iran’s oil minister has resigned days after allegations that an intermediary trust selling Iranian oil abroad owed millions of dollars’ worth of export receipts to the state.

Mohsen Paknejad’s departure comes as Iran grapples with a dire economic situation, including inflation running at 85%. articles.title: Pakistan and Turkey to provide military support to Saudi Arabia amid war with Houthis
articles.summary:
Pakistan and Turkey to provide military support to Saudi Arabia amid war with Houthis

In a joint statement issued by the Makkah Alliance, Pakistan and Turkey announced that they would provide military support to Saudi Arabia amid its war with the Houthis, following the emergency meeting of the Political Strategy and Defence Committee of the alliance.

"The Committee decided to move immediately to practical implementation of collective defence commitments and taking the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia," the statement shared by the Pakistani, Turkish, and Saudi foreign ministries said.

"The Parties affirmed that the security of each Party is an integral part of the collective security of the three countries," the statement added.

articles.title: Makkah alliance to activate 'collective deterrence', Saudi Arabia's minister of defence announces
articles.summary:
Makkah alliance to activate 'collective deterrence', Saudi Arabia's minister of defence announces

Saudi Minister of Defence Prince Khaled bin Salman announced that the Makkah alliance will activate "collective deterrence" amid the current escalation with the Houthis in Yemen, following an emergency meeting of the alliance's Strategic Political and Defence Committee in Riyadh.

The meeting "reaffirmed the solidarity and unity of our countries in confronting the heinous attacks against the Kingdom and the holy sites", the statement added.

articles.title: Yemen: Video shows armoured vehicle ramming unarmed and armed men as fighting rages
articles.summary:
Yemen: Video shows armoured vehicle ramming unarmed and armed men as fighting rages

Submitted by MEE staff on Mon, 10/05/2026 - 17:46
The vehicle mows down men who clearly have their hands raised to surrender, in addition to men armed with rifles
Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces ride in the back of a military truck at the Jabal Han front, west of the city of Taiz, following fierce battles earlier in the day, on 3 October 2026 (Ahmad al-Basha/AFP)
Off

Multiple videos have emerged on social media showing what appear to be Yemeni-government-aligned soldiers in an armoured vehicle driving over bodies and armed and unarmed men amid a counter-offensive against the Houthis.

One video shows the driver of the armoured vehicle moving into a crowd of men, some armed with rifles but others clearly holding up their hands to surrender. 

The driver clearly mows the vehicle into two men who have their arms raised to surrender. The driver and his companion then scream “Allahu Akbar” as they drive over several prone men on the side of the road; some lie motionless, and others twitch their legs. The camera's movements capture the thumps of the vehicle hitting the bodies.

At the beginning of the video, one can hear the click-clack of small arms fire, although it is not clear who is shooting.

A second video appears to show a man on the ground pointing an assault rifle at the vehicle as it comes towards him. Small arms fire can be heard in the background. After hitting the first man, the driver takes the vehicle into a crowd of men who are lying on the ground. The men raise their weapons and begin to shoot at the vehicle as it accelerates towards them.

A third video appears to show the vehicle searching for men to ram after engaging the last group. The driver finds an armed man lying alone on the beach. The driver shouts “this dog” - an Arabic curse word - before running him over. The vehicle stops, and at least one person inside the car appears to start shooting at men walking slowly on the beach who do not appear to be firing back. Several men on the beach drop, as they appear to be shot from firing emanating from the vehicle.

Middle East Eye could not independently verify the drivers of the vehicle or the armed and unarmed men the driver chases, although open-source analysts said the vehicle appeared to be operated by soldiers belonging to Yemen's government. 

Saudi-backed offensive

The videos come after Yemen’s internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia, began a counter-offensive to retake Red Sea coastal territory that the Houthis, who are aligned with Iran, captured last month.

The Yemeni government announced on Sunday that the campaign's overall objective is to retake all of the territory it lost to the Houthis in 12 years of war.

Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies began attacking Houthi positions on Monday. By evening local time, they announced taking back the Arabian Gulf side of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and Mocha, the strategic Red Sea port city that the Houthis had wrested from them in September. 

Saudi Arabia turns to UAE 'white horse' as it gears up to battle Yemen's Houthis
Read More »

The ramming videos were just some of the footage that appeared on social media showing the chaotic fighting for Yemen’s coastal strip of land known as the Tihamah Plain.

Several videos appeared to show teenage boys recruited to fight by the Houthis, captured by forces aligned with Yemen’s government.

Yemen has been wracked by conflict since the Houthis captured the country’s capital, Sanaa, in 2014, sparking a civil war. Saudi Arabia and the UAE intervened the following year to oust the Houthis from power, supporting the Yemeni government based in Aden.

A fragile United Nations-backed ceasefire struck in 2022 between Yemen’s government and the Houthis collapsed in July.

The Houthis' advance down the Red Sea added a new global dimension to the conflict, with the group declaring an embargo against Saudi vessels in the Red Sea.

The waterway is a vital corridor for the kingdom's oil shipments, with the US and Iran battling for control of the Strait of Hormuz.

The US mission in Saudi Arabia issued a security alert for American citizens in the kingdom amid the ongoing escalations with the Houthis in Yemen.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia has right to defend itself from Houthi attacks, says Rubio
articles.summary:
Saudi Arabia has right to defend itself from Houthi attacks, says Rubio

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said that Saudi Arabia has the "right to defend" itself from Houthi attacks.

Speaking to reporters in Maryland on Monday, Rubio said: “Obviously the Saudis have come under Houthi attack … and they have a right to defend themselves.”

The Republican senator said neither Saudi Arabia or Yemen's internationally recognised government were “in favour of [Houthi] control in that territory”.

Rubio also stressed that the US has a binding security agreement with Saudi Arabia and intends to honour it.

articles.title: Yemen's Saudi-backed forces begin 'strategic offensive' in Sanaa
articles.summary:
Yemen's Saudi-backed forces begin 'strategic offensive' in Sanaa

Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces said on Monday that they had begun a “strategic offensive” in Yemen's capital Sanaa.

The Iran-aligned Houthis have held the capital and vast parts of the northwest, where most of the population live, since 2014.

Saudi-backed troops also said they had seized key positions around the Bab al-Mandab strait, as they try and regain ground lost to the Houthis.
